page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-30-lssd is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 30 dedicated vCPUs spanning 15 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It integrates 240.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and bundles 804 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across two drives without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results show solid single-core throughput, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25% at 2864.57, complemented by strong PassMark memory performance at 2792.8. Most general computing metrics, including multi-core stress-ng (43041.35), PassMark CPU score (41445.01), and Geekbench multi-core (14292.0), demonstrate standard mid-tier execution. In application evaluations, the system handled 38.76 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 21.89 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge primarily in uncached memory write throughput, where large-block uncached writes registered 25.09 GB/sec, placing it in the lower 25% bracket despite respectable read speeds of 72.09 GB/sec. The bundled NVMe storage and high memory capacity provide solid local I/O performance and cache capacity, making it a cost-efficient resource tier for workloads demanding high memory density rather than extreme write-heavy bus bandwidth.

This server profile is technically configured for in-memory caching systems, intermediate database hosting, large-footprint data processing pipelines, and localized search indexing that leverage high RAM-to-vCPU ratios and attached NVMe scratch disks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-30-lssd is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with 30 dedicated vCPUs across 15 physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores, 240.0 GB of RAM, and 804 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The machine features an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and includes instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and VAES, with no integrated GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates top-quartile single-core compute via stress-ng and strong PassMark memory throughput, while overall multi-core and compression metrics align within mid-range percentiles. A notable bottleneck appears in large-block uncached memory writes, which score in the lower quartile despite consistent read bandwidth. Given its high RAM capacity, attached low-latency NVMe drives, and solid caching throughput, this configuration suits in-memory data stores, caching tiers like Redis, relational databases, and ETL workloads requiring significant transient local storage.
